definitions.explanation: A marker or trigger in a program or game that indicates a certain condition has been met.
In internet and otaku culture, an event or statement that foreshadows a particular outcome. Often used for cliché story developments, especially death scenes or romantic developments.

examples.japanese: このイベントのフラグを{回収|かいしゅう}しないと{先|さき}に{進|すす}めない。
examples.english: You can't progress unless you trigger this event flag.

examples.japanese: ゲームの{条件|じょうけん}フラグをすべて{満|み}たした。
examples.english: I met all the condition flags in the game.

examples.japanese: それ{死亡|しぼう}フラグだよ。
「この{戦|たたか}いが{終|お}わったら{結婚|けっこん}するんだ」は{完全|かんぜん}にフラグだ。
examples.english: "When this battle is over, I'm going to get married" is a total death flag.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{自分|じぶん}でフラグを{立|た}てておいて、{見事|みごと}に{回収|かいしゅう}した。
examples.english: He set up the flag himself and then perfectly followed through on it.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 2 is the more distinctively Japanese usage. フラグが{立|た}つ (a flag is raised) means a foreshadowing event has occurred. フラグを{回収|かいしゅう}する (to collect a flag) means the foreshadowed event actually happens.

TYPES:
- {死亡|しぼう}フラグ: death flag — when a character says or does something that foreshadows their death
- {恋愛|れんあい}フラグ: romance flag — an event that foreshadows a romantic development
- {生存|せいぞん}フラグ: survival flag — signs a character will survive

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- フラグが{立|た}つ: a flag is raised (foreshadowing occurs)
- フラグを{回収|かいしゅう}する: to follow through on foreshadowing
- フラグを{折|お}る: to break a flag (avoid the foreshadowed outcome)
- フラグを{立|た}てる: to set up foreshadowing
